title: Builder and ExecutionContext
sub: Who builds the task and what travels across await
cards/0/body: The state machine doesn't create the task itself. A builder does: AsyncTaskMethodBuilder<T>. It creates the Task, subscribes MoveNext to the awaiter and at the end calls SetResult or SetException.
cards/1/q: An exception is thrown inside an async method. What does the builder do?
cards/1/options/0: Calls SetException: the task becomes Faulted, and await will throw the exception
cards/1/explain: The exception rides inside the task until someone awaits it.
cards/2/body: Along with the continuation, .NET carries the ExecutionContext: the current culture, AsyncLocal<T> values and other "ambient" data. That's why AsyncLocal is still visible after await, even if a different thread runs the continuation.
cards/3/q: What does Log print after the await?
cards/3/explain: ExecutionContext carried the AsyncLocal value along with the continuation.
cards/4/q: How is ExecutionContext different from SynchronizationContext?
cards/4/options/0: ExecutionContext is data that travels with code; SynchronizationContext is where execution resumes
cards/4/explain: ConfigureAwait(false) turns off the return to the SynchronizationContext, but ExecutionContext still flows.
cards/5/body: A [ThreadStatic] field belongs to a thread: if another thread resumes the code after await, the value "vanishes". For per-request or per-operation data, use AsyncLocal.
cards/5/deep: If a called async method changes an AsyncLocal, the caller doesn't see the change after it returns: ExecutionContext is immutable and copied on write. Values flow down the call chain, not up.
cards/6/q: What flows across await with the ExecutionContext? Select all that apply.
cards/6/explain: ThreadStatic stays with its own thread.
cards/7/pairs/2/1: Per-thread data, lost on a thread switch
